This section lists the all the functions exported by **OpenSIPS** core for script usage (to be used in opensips.cfg)

functions.name: add_local_rport
functions.description: Add 'rport' parameter to the Via header generated by server (see RFC3581 for its meaning). It affects only the current processed request.

functions.name: assert
functions.description: Only works if enable_asserts is set to true. If the given expression evaluates to false, script execution is stopped and the error_route is executed. If abort_on_assert is enabled, OpenSIPS will also shutdown.

functions.name: append_branch

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: URI to copy into a new branch

functions.description: TO BECOME OBSOLETE, replaced by append_msg_branch(). Adds a new message branch, so it extends the destination set by a new entry. The difference is that current URI is taken as new entry.

functions.name: append_msg_branch

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: The 'inherite' optional flag may dictate if the other branch properties are to be inherited from the RURI branch or not.

functions.description: Adds a new message branch. The minimal information is the SIP URI of the branch. Optional, a q value may be provided. The "inherite" optional flag may dictate if the other branch properties (duri, q, path, socket, bflags) are to be inherited from the RURI branch or not.

functions.name: avp_print
functions.description: Prints the list with all the AVPs from memory. This is only a helper/debug function.

functions.name: cache_store
functions.description: This sets in a memory-cache-like storage system a new value for an attribute. If the attribute does not already exist in the memcache, it will be inserted with the given value; if already present, its value will be replaced with the new one. Function returns true if the new attribute was successfully inserted.

functions.name: cache_remove
functions.description: This removes an attribute from a memory-cache-like storage system. Function returns false only if the storage_id is invalid.

functions.name: cache_fetch
functions.description: Fetch the value of an attribute from a memory-cache-like storage system. On a successful fetch, the result will be stored in the variable specified by result_pv. Function returns true if the attribute was found and its value successfully returned.

functions.name: cache_counter_fetch
functions.description: This function fetches from a memory-cache-like storage system the value of a counter. The result (if any) will be stored in the variable specified by result. Function returns true if the attribute was found and its value returned.

functions.name: cache_add

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: if greater than 0, the key will also expire in the specified number of seconds

parameters.name: new_val
parameters.description: variable in which to fetch the new value of the counter

functions.description: This increments an attribute in a memory-cache-like storage system that supports such an operation. If the attribute does not exit, it will be created with the value of increment. Function returns false if increment fails.

functions.name: cache_sub

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: if greater than 0, the key will also expire in the specified number of seconds

parameters.name: new_val
parameters.description: variable in which to fetch the new value of the counter

functions.description: This decrements an attribute in a memory-cache-like storage system that supports such an operation. Function returns false if decrement fails.

functions.name: cache_raw_query

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: AVP (or AVP list) to store results

functions.description: The function runs the provided raw query (in the back-end dependent language) and returns the results (if any) in the AVP (or AVP list) provided in result. Function returns false if query fails.

functions.name: break
functions.description: Since v0.10.0-dev3, 'break' can no longer be used to stop the execution of a route. The only place to use is to end a 'case' block in a 'switch' statement. 'return' must be now used instead of old 'break'.

functions.name: construct_uri
functions.description: The function builds a valid sip uri based on the arguments it receives. The result (if any) will be stored in the result AVP variable.

functions.name: drop
functions.description: Stop the execution of the configuration script and alter the implicit action which is done afterwards. If the function is called in a 'branch_route' then the branch is discarded. If the function is called in a 'onreply_route' then any provisional reply is discarded.

functions.name: exit
functions.description: Stop the execution of the configuration script -- it has the same behaviour as return(0). It does not affect the implicit action to be taken after script execution.

functions.name: force_rport
functions.description: Force_rport() adds the rport parameter to the first Via header. Thus, OpenSIPS will add the received IP port to the top most via header in the SIP message, even if the client does not indicate support for rport.

functions.name: force_send_socket
functions.description: Force OpenSIPS to send the message from the specified socket (it _must_ be one of the sockets OpenSIPS listens on). If the protocol doesn't match the closest socket of the same protocol is used.

functions.name: force_tcp_alias
functions.description: Enables TCP connection reusage (RFC 5923) for the current TLS (or WSS, TCP, WS) connection (source IP + source port + transport), regardless if the Via header field contains an ";alias" parameter or not.

functions.name: forward

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: if missing, the forward will be done based on RURI.

functions.description: Forward the SIP request to the given destination in stateless mode. This has the format of [proto:]host[:port].

functions.name: get_timestamp
functions.description: Returns the current timestamp, seconds and microseconds of the current second, from a single system call.

functions.name: isdsturiset
functions.description: Test if the dst_uri field (next hop address) is set.

functions.name: isflagset
functions.description: Test if a flag is set for currently processed message.

functions.name: isbflagset
functions.description: Test if a flag is set for a specific branch. "branch_idx" identifies the branch for which the flags are tested - it must be a positive number.

examples.code:
if (isbflagset(1, "NAT_PING"))
    log("flag NAT_PING is set in branch 1\n");

functions.name: is_myself
functions.description: Test if the host and optionally the port represent one of the addresses that OpenSIPS listens on.

examples.code:
if (is_myself($rd, $rp)
    xlog("the request is for local processing\n");

functions.name: log
functions.description: Write text message to standard error terminal or syslog. You can specify the log level as first parameter.

functions.name: move_branch

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: If 'keep', the branch is not removed, only copied

functions.description: Moves the whole information attached to the src_idx branch to the dst_idx branch.

functions.name: next_branches
functions.description: Adds to the request a new destination set that includes all highest priority class contacts ('q' value based) from the serialized branches (see serialize_branches()). Returns true if at least one contact was added for the request's destination set - returns 1 if other branches are still pending and return 2 if no other branches are left for future processing.

functions.name: prefix
functions.description: Add the string parameter in front of username in R-URI.

functions.name: pv_printf
functions.description: Prints the formatted string 'fmt_str' in the AVP 'pv'. The 'fmt_str' parameter can include any pseudo-variable defined in OpenSIPS.

functions.name: raise_event

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: the name of the event which should be raised

parameters.name: attrs
parameters.description: AVP containing the the names of the attributes

parameters.name: vals
parameters.description: AVP containing values attached to the event

functions.description: Raises from script an event through OpenSIPS Event Interface. This function triggers an event for all subscribers for that event, regardless the transport module used.

examples.description: Example of usage (raises an event with no attributes)
Example of usage (raises an event with two attributes)
Example of usage (raises an event with two unnamed attributes)

functions.name: remove_msg_branch
functions.description: Removes a given branch. Once a branch is removed, all the subsequent branches are shifted.

examples.description: Example of usage (remove all branches with URI hostname "127.0.0.1")

functions.name: return
functions.description: The return() function allows you to return any integer value from a called route() block. You can test the value returned by a route using "$retcode" variable.

functions.name: resetdsturi
functions.description: Set the value of dst_uri filed to NULL. dst_uri field is usually set after loose_route() or lookup("location") if the contact address is behind a NAT.

functions.name: resetflag
functions.description: Reset a flag for currently processed message (unset its value).

functions.name: resetbflag
functions.description: Reset a flag for a specific branch (unset its value). "branch_idx" identifies the branch for which the flag is reset - it must be a positive number.

functions.name: revert_uri
functions.description: Set the R-URI to the value of the R-URI as it was when the request was received by server (undo all changes of R-URI).

functions.name: set_via_handling

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: a comma separated list of named flags

functions.description: Rewrite the domain part of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter. Other parts of the R-URI like username, port and URI parameters remain unchanged.

functions.name: sethost
functions.description: Rewrite the domain part of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter. Other parts of the R-URI like username, port and URI parameters remain unchanged.

functions.name: sethostport
functions.description: Rewrite the domain part and port of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter. Other parts of the R-URI like username and URI parameters remain unchanged.

functions.name: setuser
functions.description: Rewrite the user part of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter.

functions.name: setuserpass
functions.description: Rewrite the password part of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter.

functions.name: setport
functions.description: Rewrites/sets the port part of the R-URI with the value of function's parameter.

functions.name: seturi
functions.description: Rewrite the request URI.

functions.name: route
functions.description: This function is used to run the code from the 'name' route, declared in the script. Optionally, it can receive several parameters (up to 7), that can be later retrieved using the '$param(idx)' pseudo-variable.

functions.name: script_trace
functions.description: This function start the script tracing - this helps to better understand the flow of execution in the OpenSIPS script, like what function is executed, what line it is, etc.

functions.name: send
functions.description: Send the original SIP message to a specific destination in stateless mode. This is definied as [proto:]host[:port].

functions.name: serialize_branches

parameters.name: clear_previous
parameters.description: if set to non-zero, all previous results... will be deleted

parameters.name: keep_order
parameters.description: if set to non-zero, the added branches... will be serialized exactly in the order in which they are found.

functions.description: Takes all currently added branches for parallel forking (e.g. with lookup() or append_branch()), as well as the current branch (R-URI ($ru) / outbound Proxy ($du) / q value ($ru_q) / branch flags / forced Path headers / forced send socket), and prepares them for serial forking instead.

functions.name: set_advertised_address
functions.description: Same as 'advertised_address' but it affects only the current message. It has priority if 'advertised_address' is also set.

functions.name: set_advertised_port
functions.description: Same as 'advertised_port' but it affects only the current message. It has priority over 'advertised_port'.

functions.name: setdsturi
functions.description: Explicitely set the dst_uri field to the value of the paramater. The parameter has to be a valid SIP URI.

functions.name: setflag
functions.description: Set a flag for currently processed message. The flags are used to mark the message for special processing (e.g. pinging NAT'ed contacts, TCP connect behavior, etc.) or to keep some state (e.g. message authenticated).

functions.name: setbflag
functions.description: Set a flag for a specific branch. "branch_idx" identifies the branch for which the flag is set - it must be a positive number.

functions.name: socket_belongs_to_bond

parameters.name: bond
parameters.description: the name of a bond socket

functions.description: This function checks if a SIP socket is part of a certain bond socket (see the definition of a bond socket).

functions.name: sr_check_status

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: the name of the identifier to be checked

functions.description: Function to check the status of an 'status/report' identifier. Such checking is very useful for determining at script level the readiness of a module or core component (if able to provide its full functionality).

functions.name: strip
functions.description: Strip the first N-th characters from username of R-URI (N is the value of the parameter).

functions.name: strip_tail
functions.description: Strip the last N-th characters from username of R-URI (N is the value of the parameter).

functions.name: subscribe_event

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: the name of the event an external application should be notified for.

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: the socket of the external application.

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: the expire time of the subscription.

functions.description: Subscribes an external application for a certain event for the OpenSIPS Event Interface. This is used for transport protocols that cannot subscribe by themselves (example event_rabbitmq).

examples.description: Example of usage (subscriber that never expires, notified by the RabbitMQ module)
Example of usage (subscriber expires every 5 seconds, notified through UDP)

functions.name: swap_branches
functions.description: Swaps the information between two branches, represented by the br1_idx and br2_idx. Both values should be an integer value and should represent a valid branch index.

functions.name: use_blacklist
functions.description: Enables the DNS blacklist name received as parameter. Its primary purposes will be to prevent sending requests to critical IPs (like GWs) due DNS or to avoid sending to destinations that are known to be unavailable (temporary or permanent).

functions.name: unuse_blacklist
functions.description: Disables the DNS blacklist name received as parameter.

functions.name: check_blacklist_rule

parameters.name: bl_name
parameters.description: if missing, the rule is matched against all used blacklists

functions.description: Checks whether a specific proto:ip:port+pattern matches a blacklist, or all if bl_name is not specified.

functions.name: add_blacklist_rule

parameters.name: bl_name
parameters.description: the blacklist to add the rule to

functions.description: Adds a proto:ip:port+pattern rule to a blacklist.

functions.name: del_blacklist_rule

parameters.name: bl_name
parameters.description: the blacklist to remove the rule from

functions.description: Removes a proto:ip:port+pattern rule from a blacklist.

functions.name: xlog
functions.description: Allows various debugging / runtime / critical messages to be printed as the execution of the OpenSIPS script is done. All pseudo-variables included in the format_string parameter will be expanded.
